questions.cardText:
[Economics] Which of the following variables is the most predictive of a country’s consumption of luxury goods?
A. Unemployment rate
B. Marginal tax rate
C. Income inequality
Answer: C. In countries with high income inequality, wealthier individuals tend to spend more on luxury items to display their status and distinguish themselves from lower-income groups. This trend drives the overall demand for high-end products in such economies.
questions.en: What term, coined by Thorstein Veblen, describes spending on luxury goods to display one’s wealth and social status?
questions.de: Welcher von Thorstein Veblen geprägte Begriff bezeichnet das Ausgeben von Geld für Luxusgüter, um Reichtum und sozialen Status zur Schau zu stellen?

timeline.labelEn: Thorstein Veblen coins “conspicuous consumption” in The Theory of the Leisure Class
timeline.labelDe: Thorstein Veblen prägt in „The Theory of the Leisure Class“ den Begriff „conspicuous consumption“

questions.notes: The card's claim that income inequality is 'the most predictive' variable is a debatable empirical generalisation that only works among its three options; asked instead the underlying idea its explanation gives (status display through luxury spending = Veblen's conspicuous consumption).

questions.cardText:
[Religious Studies] Where was Buddha born?
A. Nepal  B. Bangladesh  C. India
Answer: A. Siddhartha Gautama, who later became known as Buddha, was born in Lumbini, which is located in present-day Nepal.
questions.en: In which present-day country was Siddhartha Gautama, the Buddha, born?
questions.de: In welchem heutigen Land wurde Siddhartha Gautama, der Buddha, geboren?

timeline.labelEn: Traditional date of Siddhartha Gautama's birth in Lumbini
timeline.labelDe: Überliefertes Geburtsjahr Siddhartha Gautamas in Lumbini

questions.notes: Birthplace Lumbini (Rupandehi District, Nepal) per sacred texts; the birth year c. 563 BCE is traditional and disputed.
